data.text/markdown:
Linear Gaussian Collateral Model: calibration

A two-currency market, USD (domestic d, collateral SOFR) and EUR (foreign f, collateral ESTR, index EURIBOR 3M), with the collateral basis c (f to d) and the FX rate x (USD per EUR). The quotes are rounded broker-screen style numbers, not live data. What is calibrated to what (algorithm "LGCM calibration" of the notes):
  1. ||(Z^{d|d}||), ||(Z^{f|f}||) from the swaps (model-free bootstrap).
  2. ||(\lambda^d||), ||(\lambda^f||) (piecewise constant) from the ATM swaption normal vols, expiry by expiry.
  3. A fixed point: ||(Z^{f|d}||) from the FX forwards and resetting CCS (using the LGCM Libor convexities, which depend on ||(\sigma^c||)), then ||(\lambda^c||) from the currency-basis spread vols, repeated until neither moves.
  4. ||(\sigma^x||) from the ATM FX vols (the total variance is quadratic in ||(\sigma^x||) on each segment).
  5. Model output, not an input: the off-market curve ||(Z^{d|f}||) (USD cash flows collateralised in EUR).
Exact versus approximate. With one factor per block the swaption vols are priced exactly (quadrature); the Gaussian approximation of the swaption variance is only used as the starting guess and is asymptotic in the volatility, its error is shown in the approx column below. The multi-factor case uses the Gaussian approximation. Mean reversions and correlations are marked inputs, not calibrated. The Monte Carlo check is a statistical statement: model minus market should lie within 4 standard errors.

data.text/html:
Market quotes

FX spot 1.1000 USD per EUR; 65 quotes.

Controls

The sliders recalibrate the whole model (about 7 s) when released (results are cached per parameter tuple, so returning to earlier values is instant). The Monte Carlo check and the parameter-impact table (up to 5 recalibrations) run only on their buttons.

data.text/markdown:
Calibration

Calibrated in 7.2 s (cached: a repeated parameter tuple is not recalibrated); fixed point (||(Z^{f|d}||), ||(\sigma^c||)) converged in 5 iterations (max change per iteration: inf, 6.2e-04, 1.8e-07, 4.0e-11, 8.3e-15). Parameters: ||(\rho^{fc}||) = -0.4, CB vol scale = 1.0, ||(\beta^c||) = 0.10, ||(\beta^f||) = 0.02. DCB = the same quotes with deterministic collateral basis (no convexity).

data.text/html: Calibrated curves and volatilities

Analytic repricing

The model reprices every quote with the exact pricer; the largest absolute error (in the unit of the row) is 1.5e-12. The last column is the error of the Gaussian approximation for swaption and CB vols, which is asymptotic in the volatility (not exact), so it is nonzero.

Monte Carlo check

Press Run Monte Carlo check above. Note: the result is cleared whenever the model is recalibrated (a slider is released), because this cell depends on the calibration and the button resets after each run; press the button again for the new model.

data.text/html:
Collateral convexity

All numbers are computed from the calibrated model. Under the current parameters:
  • 30Y ||(Z^{f|d}||) zero-rate shift, LGCM minus DCB: 3.75 bp
  • 10Y FX forward collateral convexity ||(x^{df|f}/x^{df|d}-1||): 15.30 bp (30Y: 119.58 bp)
  • 10Y ||(Z^{d|f}||) zero-rate difference to the DCB off-market curve: 1.53 bp
  • Largest Libor convexity ||(K_j-1||) over 30Y: 2.24 bp at 29.75Y
The DCB curves ignore the stochastic basis; the differences are the convexity adjustments that the LGCM adds. They are exact closed forms of the calibrated Gaussian model (no Monte Carlo noise).
